title: Post-doctoral Fellow (HKU Stone Centre on Socio-Economic Inequality in Asia)
description:
Applications are invited for appointment as Post-doctoral Fellow at
the James M. and Cathleen D. Stone Centre on Socio-Economic
Inequality in Asia, jointly hosted by the Faculty of Social
Sciences and the HKU Business School. The appointment will commence
in 2027 on a one- to three-year temporary contract, with the
possibility of renewal subject to funding availability and
satisfactory performance.

About the Centre The James M. and Cathleen D. Stone
Centre on Socio-Economic Inequality in Asia at the University of
Hong Kong is dedicated to the comparative study of income and
wealth inequality in Asia. As the first Stone Centre in Asia, it
connects researchers across disciplines and geographies to
understand the nature, causes, and consequences of inequality, and
to compare Asian experiences with those of North America and
Europe. The Centre emphasises rigorous measurement, causal
analysis, and clear communication of research findings. It is a
joint initiative of the Faculty of Social Sciences and the
Economics Department at HKU Business School, co-directed by
Professor Tarani Chandola, Professor Uta Schönberg, and Professor
Ming Wen.

The Applicant
We are seeking a highly motivated researcher with a PhD degree in
economics or a related discipline, specialising in labour
economics, trade, development, or political economy. The ideal
candidate will have substantial experience working with large-scale
datasets, including unstructured data such as LinkedIn data or job
advertisements, as well as expertise in web crawling, large
language models, and text analysis techniques. A strong
understanding of causal inference methods is essential for
developing rigorous research insights.

Proficiency in both written and spoken English is required;
proficiency in written and spoken Chinese is advantageous but not
essential. The ability to work both independently and
collaboratively within a team is crucial.

Key duties include conducting quantitative and qualitative data
analyses, preparing manuscripts for publication in high-impact
academic journals, and presenting research findings at research
institutions and conferences. Fellows will be paired with a mentor
from the Centre's leadership team for guidance and support. In
addition, they will assist team leaders with project management
tasks and contribute to the Centre's strategic planning and daily
activities to ensure smooth operations.

A competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and
experience will be offered, along with annual leave and medical
benefits.

Review of applications will begin as soon as possible and continue
until January 15, 2027, or until the post is filled, whichever is
earlier. Inquiries about the post should be sent to stonecentre@hku.hk .

The University is an equal opportunities employer
and
is committed to equality, ethics, inclusivity, diversity and
transparency

Advertised: Oct 14, 2026 (HK Time)
Applications close: Jan 15, 2027 (HK Time)
